diff --git a/base/.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh b/head/.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh
index cf77799..751cec7 100644
--- a/base/.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh
+++ b/head/.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh
@@ -164,6 +164,14 @@ load_adversarial_config() {
   CONF_SECRET_ALLOWLIST=()  # Patterns that should NOT be redacted
   # cycle-124 FR-7: the KF-004 repair loop has no flag any more — it always
   # runs on the UNENFORCED branch and never on a schema-enforced payload.
+  # cycle-129 FR-7 (D-7.4): advisory voices — run after the counted voices, findings only under advisory_voices[]
+  CONF_ADVISORY_VOICES=""       # space-separated aliases (default none)
+  CONF_ADVISORY_TIMEOUT=600     # one wall clock for all of them
+  CONF_PROMOTION_MIN_RECALL=""  # hounfour.advisory_promotion.* — read and named; promotion is unreachable this cycle
+  CONF_PROMOTION_MAX_REFUTED=""
+  # cycle-129 FR-8 (D-8.1): hounfour.locality — hosted (default, the rollback) | local_voices | invalid (refused in main)
+  CONF_LOCALITY="hosted"
+  CONF_LOCALITY_RAW=""
 
   if [[ ! -f "$CONFIG_FILE" ]]; then
     log "Config file not found, using defaults"
@@ -220,6 +228,25 @@ load_adversarial_config() {
   fi
   CONF_COMPANION_CHAIN_ANTHROPIC=$(_adv_conf_chain_hops "$config_key" anthropic)
   CONF_COMPANION_CHAIN_OPENAI=$(_adv_conf_chain_hops "$config_key" openai)
+  # cycle-129 FR-7 (D-7.4): advisory voices and their one wall clock; FR-8 (D-8.1): the locality switch. Neither is a
+  # profile key — read here, never through loa_knob (sprint.md Sprint 3, Implementers note).
+  CONF_ADVISORY_VOICES=$(_adv_conf_advisory_voices "$config_key")
+  CONF_ADVISORY_TIMEOUT=$(yq eval ".flatline_protocol.${config_key}.advisory_timeout_seconds // 600" "$CONFIG_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo "600")
+  CONF_ADVISORY_TIMEOUT=$(_conf_uint "flatline_protocol.${config_key}.advisory_timeout_seconds" "$CONF_ADVISORY_TIMEOUT" 600 1)
+  CONF_PROMOTION_MIN_RECALL=$(yq eval '.hounfour.advisory_promotion.min_recall_ratio // ""' "$CONFIG_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true)
+  CONF_PROMOTION_MAX_REFUTED=$(yq eval '.hounfour.advisory_promotion.max_refuted_delta // ""' "$CONFIG_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true)
+  local _loct _locv
+  _loct=$(yq eval '.hounfour.locality | tag' "$CONFIG_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo "unreadable")
+  case "$_loct" in
+    '!!null'|'') CONF_LOCALITY="hosted" ;;
+    '!!str')
+      _locv=$(yq eval '.hounfour.locality' "$CONFIG_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
+      case "$_locv" in
+        hosted|local_voices) CONF_LOCALITY="$_locv" ;;
+        *) CONF_LOCALITY="invalid"; CONF_LOCALITY_RAW=$(printf '%s' "$_locv" | LC_ALL=C tr -cd 'A-Za-z0-9._-' | cut -c1-40) ;;
+      esac ;;
+    *) CONF_LOCALITY="invalid"; CONF_LOCALITY_RAW="(a ${_loct#!!}, not a string)" ;;
+  esac
   CONF_ESCALATION_ENABLED=$(yq eval ".flatline_protocol.context_escalation.enabled // true" "$CONFIG_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo "true")
   CONF_SECONDARY_BUDGET=$(yq eval ".flatline_protocol.context_escalation.secondary_token_budget // $DEFAULT_SECONDARY_TOKEN_BUDGET" "$CONFIG_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo "$DEFAULT_SECONDARY_TOKEN_BUDGET")
   CONF_MAX_FILE_LINES=$(yq eval ".flatline_protocol.context_escalation.max_file_lines // 500" "$CONFIG_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo "500")
@@ -657,6 +684,12 @@ _repair_chain_base() {  # <voice that answered> → the repair chain before the
   # PATH, and the voice that answered ALWAYS last — an OpenAI-only host without `claude` repairs through
   # its own primary (the cycle-119 C14 behaviour) instead of failing every KF-004 payload deterministically.
   # An operator pin (LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REPAIR_MODEL) is the whole chain.
+  # cycle-129 FR-8 (D-8.1): under hounfour.locality: local_voices the chain is the answering voice alone — no tiny, no
+  # claude-headless, no pin — and only when that voice is itself a local hop; otherwise there is no repair hop at all
+  if [[ "${CONF_LOCALITY:-hosted}" == "local_voices" ]]; then
+    if [[ -n "$1" ]] && _adv_hop_is_local "$1"; then echo "$1"; else echo ""; fi
+    return 0
+  fi
   local _pin; _pin=$(_adv_repair_pin)
   if [[ -n "$_pin" ]]; then echo "$_pin"; return 0; fi
   local chain=""
@@ -673,6 +706,9 @@ _repair_chain_base() {  # <voice that answered> → the repair chain before the
 }
 _repair_model_chain() {  # <voice that answered> → the repair chain, one bounded attempt per hop (the base chain, filtered)
   local chain; chain=$(_repair_chain_base "$1")
+  # (cycle-129 D-8.1: under local_voices the base chain is final — never the `${chain:-$1}` fallback below, which would
+  # name a voice the base refused)
+  if [[ "${CONF_LOCALITY:-hosted}" == "local_voices" ]]; then echo "$chain"; return 0; fi
   if [[ -n "$(_adv_repair_pin)" ]]; then
     # twentieth run, a1 DISS-C-002: a pin is the whole chain, but a pinned hop retired this run is not paid for again — an
     # entirely retired pin is an empty chain (the payload is then repair_skipped_no_hop), never the answering voice
@@ -3757,6 +3793,241 @@ _adv_prev_files_drop() {  # the previous run's envelope and sidecars moved aside
   done <<<"${_ADV_PREV_FILES:-}"
   return 0
 }
+# =============================================================================
+# cycle-129 FR-7 / FR-8 (SDD D-7.4, D-7.6, D-8.1): advisory voices, the catalog-priced budget gate, locality
+# =============================================================================
+
+_adv_conf_advisory_voices() {  # <config key> → flatline_protocol.<key>.advisory_voices' hop names, space-separated (first
+  # occurrence kept); a non-list is said and ignored, an element that is not a hop name is said (by index and tag, never its
+  # value) and dropped — _adv_conf_chain_hops' rule. (Only the gate's own config key is spliced into the yq expressions.)
+  local config_key="$1" label="flatline_protocol.$1.advisory_voices" tg n rows="" out="" i v _nr=0
+  tg=$(yq eval ".flatline_protocol.${config_key}.advisory_voices | tag" "$CONFIG_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true)
+  [[ -z "$tg" || "$tg" == "!!null" ]] && return 0
+  if [[ "$tg" != "!!seq" ]]; then log "WARN: ${label} is a ${tg#!!}, not a list of aliases — ignored"; return 0; fi
+  n=$(yq eval ".flatline_protocol.${config_key}.advisory_voices | length" "$CONFIG_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true)
+  if [[ ! "$n" =~ ^[0-9]{1,2}$ ]]; then log "WARN: ${label} could not be read or has over 99 entries — ignored"; return 0; fi
+  (( n == 0 )) && return 0
+  rows=$(yq -o=json -I=0 eval ".flatline_protocol.${config_key}.advisory_voices[] | [tag, .]" "$CONFIG_FILE" 2>/dev/null \
+    | jq -rn '[inputs] | to_entries[]
+        | (.value[0] | if type == "string" and test("\\A[!A-Za-z0-9._/:-]{1,64}\\z") then . else "unreadable" end) as $tg
+        | if $tg == "!!str" and (.value[1] | type) == "string" and (.value[1] | test("\\A[A-Za-z0-9._/:-]{1,128}\\z"))
+          then "\(.key) ok \(.value[1])" else "\(.key) drop \($tg)" end' 2>/dev/null) || rows=""
+  [[ -z "$rows" ]] || _nr=$(grep -c '' <<<"$rows")
+  if [[ "$_nr" != "$n" ]]; then log "WARN: ${label} could not be read — ignored"; return 0; fi
+  while read -r i tg v; do
+    [[ -n "$i" ]] || continue
+    if [[ "$tg" == ok ]]; then [[ " $out " == *" $v "* ]] || out+="$v "
+    else log "WARN: ${label}[$i] is not a hop name (${v:-unreadable}) — dropped"; fi
+  done <<<"$rows"
+  printf '%s' "${out% }"
+}
+
+# --- locality (D-8.1): one classification per hop, from lib/hop-locality.py over the merged catalog + project config ----
+_ADV_LOC_TSV=""       # "<hop>\t<provider>\t<local|hosted>\t<reason>" lines, this process
+_ADV_LOC_REFUSED=""   # "<role>\t<hop>\t<provider>" lines — every hosted hop refused at plan time (the envelope names them)
+_ADV_LOC_KEPT=""      # _adv_locality_filter's answer (a global: the caller runs it at top level, never in $(...))
+_adv_locality_row() { awk -F'\t' -v h="$1" '$1 == h { print; exit }' <<<"$_ADV_LOC_TSV"; }
+_adv_locality_load() {  # <hop>... — classify the hops this process has not classified yet (one python call); fail closed
+  local -a new=(); local h line rows="" cat="${LOA_MODEL_CONFIG:-$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml}"
+  for h in "$@"; do [[ -n "$h" && -z "$(_adv_locality_row "$h")" ]] && new+=("$h"); done
+  (( ${#new[@]} > 0 )) || return 0
+  rows=$(python3 -I "$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/scripts/lib/hop-locality.py" --catalog "$cat" --config "${CONFIG_FILE:-}" -- "${new[@]}" 2>/dev/null) || rows=""
+  for h in "${new[@]}"; do
+    line=$(awk -F'\t' -v h="$h" '$1 == h && NF >= 4 { print; exit }' <<<"$rows")
+    [[ -n "$line" ]] || line="${h}"$'\t'"unknown"$'\t'"hosted"$'\t'"classifier_unavailable"   # (no answer is a hosted hop)
+    _ADV_LOC_TSV+="${line}"$'\n'
+  done
+}
+_adv_hop_is_local() { _adv_locality_load "$1"; [[ "$(_adv_locality_row "$1" | cut -f3)" == "local" ]]; }
+_adv_locality_filter() {  # <role> <hop>... → _ADV_LOC_KEPT: the local hops in order; each hosted one is refused by name, once per role
+  local role="$1" h p; shift
+  _ADV_LOC_KEPT=""
+  _adv_locality_load "$@"
+  for h in "$@"; do
+    [[ -n "$h" ]] || continue
+    if [[ "$(_adv_locality_row "$h" | cut -f3)" == "local" ]]; then _ADV_LOC_KEPT+="${_ADV_LOC_KEPT:+ }$h"; continue; fi
+    p=$(_adv_locality_row "$h" | cut -f2); p="${p:-unknown}"
+    if ! grep -qxF "${role}"$'\t'"${h}"$'\t'"${p}" <<<"$_ADV_LOC_REFUSED"; then
+      _ADV_LOC_REFUSED+="${role}"$'\t'"${h}"$'\t'"${p}"$'\n'
+      log "locality: local_voices refuses hosted hop $h ($p)"
+    fi
+  done
+  return 0
+}
+_adv_locality_refused_json() {  # → [{role, alias, provider}] for the envelope
+  printf '%s' "$_ADV_LOC_REFUSED" | jq -R -s 'split("\n") | map(select(length > 0) | split("\t") | {role: .[0], alias: .[1], provider: .[2]})'
+}
+# The one sentence the config comment and the audit output carry (D-8.1).
+_ADV_LOC_DEGRADED_SENTENCE="locality: local_voices — with one local family the companion is not an independent second voice (duplicate_voice, or not planned), so every security audit is DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW; adversarial-review-gate.sh and verdict-derive.sh treat this envelope exactly as they treat any other."
+
+# --- the budget gate (D-7.4, D-7.6): every planned voice at its catalog price ------------------------------------------
+_ADV_BUDGET_TOTAL=0
+_ADV_BUDGET_VOICES="[]"
+_adv_budget_estimate() {  # <estimated input tokens> <role>=<hop>... → _ADV_BUDGET_TOTAL (cents) and _ADV_BUDGET_VOICES (JSON);
+  # each voice: input tokens × input rate + 2000 output tokens × output rate (micro-USD per Mtok → cents: ÷ 10^10, each term
+  # truncated, as the fixed-rate formula was). An alias with no catalog price falls back to 10 / 30 USD per Mtok and is said;
+  # a zero-priced one estimates 0 and is said too.
+  local tokens="$1"; shift
+  local -a roles=() hops=() args=()
+  local rv rows="" line c_in c_out total=0 voices="[]"
+  for rv in "$@"; do roles+=("${rv%%=*}"); hops+=("${rv#*=}"); args+=(--alias "${rv#*=}"); done
+  if (( ${#hops[@]} > 0 )); then
+    rows=$(PYTHONSAFEPATH=1 PYTHONPATH="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/adapters" python3 -W ignore::RuntimeWarning -m loa_cheval.metering.pricing \
+      --catalog "${LOA_MODEL_CONFIG:-$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml}" --config "${CONFIG_FILE:-}" "${args[@]}" 2>/dev/null) || rows=""
+  fi
+  local k _bv_role _bv_hop _bv_src _bv_in _bv_out _bv_cents
+  for (( k = 0; k < ${#hops[@]}; k++ )); do
+    _bv_role="${roles[$k]}"; _bv_hop="${hops[$k]}"   # (a role word and a validated hop name — the jq operands below are small)
+    line=$(awk -v a="alias=$_bv_hop" '$1 == a { print; exit }' <<<"$rows")
+    _bv_in=$(sed -n 's/.* input_per_mtok=\([0-9][0-9]*\) .*/\1/p' <<<"$line")
+    _bv_out=$(sed -n 's/.* output_per_mtok=\([0-9][0-9]*\) .*/\1/p' <<<"$line")
+    _bv_src=$(sed -n 's/.* pricing_source=\([a-z_]*\)$/\1/p' <<<"$line")
+    if [[ ! "$_bv_in" =~ ^[0-9]{1,12}$ || ! "$_bv_out" =~ ^[0-9]{1,12}$ || "$_bv_src" == "unknown" || -z "$_bv_src" ]]; then
+      _bv_in=10000000; _bv_out=30000000; _bv_src="fallback"
+      log "budget: no catalog price for $_bv_hop ($_bv_role) — the fixed 10 / 30 USD per Mtok applies to this voice"
+    elif (( _bv_in == 0 && _bv_out == 0 )); then
+      log "budget: $_bv_hop ($_bv_role) is zero-priced in the catalog — estimated 0c"
+    elif [[ "$_bv_src" == "stale_catalog" ]]; then
+      log "budget: $_bv_hop ($_bv_role) has a stale catalog price (price_date older than 90 days) — used as given"
+    fi
+    c_in=$(( tokens * _bv_in / 10000000000 )); c_out=$(( 2000 * _bv_out / 10000000000 )); _bv_cents=$(( c_in + c_out ))
+    total=$(( total + _bv_cents ))
+    voices=$(jq -c --arg r "$_bv_role" --arg h "$_bv_hop" --arg s "$_bv_src" --argjson c "$_bv_cents" --argjson i "$_bv_in" --argjson o "$_bv_out" \
+      '. + [{role: $r, alias: $h, estimated_cents: $c, input_per_mtok: $i, output_per_mtok: $o, pricing_source: $s}]' <<<"$voices")

+_adv_run_advisory_voices() {  # <type> <sprint id> <timeout> <diff files> <alias>... — every voice started at once under
+  # $CONF_ADVISORY_TIMEOUT seconds of wall clock for all of them; a voice still running then is killed and marked timed_out.

+  local type="$1" sprint_id="$2" timeout="$3" diff_files="$4"; shift 4

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""hop-locality.py — classify model hops as local or hosted for `hounfour.locality: local_voices` (cycle-129 FR-8,
SDD D-8.0 / D-8.1, DEC-0146).

    python3 -I hop-locality.py --catalog <model-config.yaml> --config <.loa.config.yaml> -- <hop>...

One tab-separated line per hop, in the order given:

    <hop> TAB <provider|unknown> TAB <local|hosted> TAB <reason>

A hop is `local` only when ALL of these hold in the merged view (the System Zone catalog overlaid with the project
config's `hounfour.providers` / `hounfour.aliases`, the two layers cheval merges):
  * it resolves (a `provider:id` pin, an alias chain, or a bare id that exactly one provider declares) to a model entry
    that exists;
  * that model entry, or its provider block, says `dispatch_group: local` (the canonical key, D-8.0);
  * every hop on the entry's own `fallback_chain` is local by the same rule — cheval walks that chain inside one call,
    so a local entry that falls back to a hosted one would leave the declared providers without the planner seeing it.
Everything else is `hosted`: an unresolved hop, an unreadable config, a headless CLI hop (its dispatch group is the
provider family's), the native session. Fail closed — a hop is never called local because it could not be read.

This file reads declarations only: it never dispatches, never reads credentials and never imports the cheval package
(run under `-I`, so neither the cwd nor PYTHONPATH reaches sys.path). The request-time rules for a local hop (IP-literal
or localhost endpoint, no DNS, redirects refused, proxy env ignored, destination logged) are cheval's.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import sys
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple

MAX_DEPTH = 10


def _merge(base: Any, overlay: Any) -> Any:
    if isinstance(base, dict) and isinstance(overlay, dict):
        out = dict(base)
        for key, value in overlay.items():
            out[key] = _merge(base.get(key), value) if key in base else value
        return out
    return overlay


def load_merged(catalog_path: str, config_path: Optional[str]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    import yaml

    with open(catalog_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        catalog = yaml.safe_load(fh) or {}
    if not isinstance(catalog, dict):
        raise ValueError("catalog is not a mapping")
    merged: Dict[str, Any] = {k: (catalog.get(k) if isinstance(catalog.get(k), dict) else {})
                              for k in ("providers", "aliases", "backward_compat_aliases")}
    if config_path:
        try:
            with open(config_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
                project = yaml.safe_load(fh) or {}
        except FileNotFoundError:
            project = {}
        if not isinstance(project, dict):
            raise ValueError("project config is not a mapping")
        hounfour = project.get("hounfour")
        if isinstance(hounfour, dict):
            for key in ("providers", "aliases"):
                if isinstance(hounfour.get(key), dict):
                    merged[key] = _merge(merged.get(key) or {}, hounfour[key])
    return merged


def _alias_target(name: str, merged: Dict[str, Any]) -> Optional[str]:
    for table in ("aliases", "backward_compat_aliases"):
        target = (merged.get(table) or {}).get(name)
        if isinstance(target, dict):
            target = target.get("target") or target.get("model")
        if isinstance(target, str) and target.strip():
            return target.strip()
    return None


def resolve(hop: str, merged: Dict[str, Any]) -> Optional[Tuple[str, str]]:
    name = (hop or "").strip()
    if not name:
        return None
    current, seen = name, set()
    for _ in range(MAX_DEPTH):
        if ":" in current:
            provider, _, model = current.partition(":")
            return (provider, model) if provider and model else None
        target = _alias_target(current, merged)
        if not target:
            break
        if target in seen:
            return None
        seen.add(current)
        current = target
    if ":" in current:
        provider, _, model = current.partition(":")
        return (provider, model) if provider and model else None
    providers = merged.get("providers") or {}
    matches = [p for p, block in providers.items()
               if isinstance(block, dict) and isinstance(block.get("models"), dict) and current in block["models"]]
    return (matches[0], current) if len(matches) == 1 else None


def classify(hop: str, merged: Dict[str, Any], _depth: int = 0, _seen: Optional[set] = None) -> Tuple[str, str, str]:
    """(provider, locality, reason) for one hop."""
    seen = set(_seen or ())
    target = resolve(hop, merged)
    if target is None:
        return "unknown", "hosted", "unresolved"
    provider, model = target
    block = (merged.get("providers") or {}).get(provider)
    if not isinstance(block, dict):
        return provider, "hosted", "provider_not_declared"
    entry = (block.get("models") or {}).get(model) if isinstance(block.get("models"), dict) else None
    if not isinstance(entry, dict):
        return provider, "hosted", "model_not_declared"
    group = entry.get("dispatch_group") or block.get("dispatch_group") or ""
    if group != "local":
        return provider, "hosted", f"dispatch_group={group or 'unset'}"
    key = f"{provider}:{model}"
    if key in seen:
        return provider, "local", "dispatch_group=local"
    seen.add(key)
    chain = entry.get("fallback_chain") or []
    if not isinstance(chain, list):
        return provider, "hosted", "fallback_chain_unreadable"
    if _depth >= MAX_DEPTH:
        return provider, "hosted", "fallback_chain_too_deep"
    for nxt in chain:
        if not isinstance(nxt, str):
            return provider, "hosted", "fallback_chain_unreadable"
        p2, loc, _ = classify(nxt, merged, _depth + 1, seen)
        if loc != "local":
            return provider, "hosted", f"fallback_chain_reaches_hosted:{nxt}({p2})"
    return provider, "local", "dispatch_group=local"


def _clean(text: str) -> str:
    return "".join(c if c.isprintable() and c not in "\t" else "_" for c in text)[:128]


def main(argv: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("--catalog", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--config", default="")
    ap.add_argument("hops", nargs="*")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        merged = load_merged(args.catalog, args.config or None)
        err = ""
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — fail closed: every hop hosted, the reason said once
        merged, err = None, f"{type(exc).__name__}"
        print(f"hop-locality: the merged config could not be read ({err}) — every hop is hosted", file=sys.stderr)
    for hop in args.hops:
        if merged is None:
            print(f"{_clean(hop)}\tunknown\thosted\tconfig_unreadable")
            continue
        provider, loc, reason = classify(hop, merged)
        print(f"{_clean(hop)}\t{_clean(provider)}\t{loc}\t{_clean(reason)}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

+STALE_PRICE_DAYS = 90
+_PRICE_DATE_RE = re.compile(r"^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$")
+_STALE_WARNED: set = set()

+def price_date_of(entry: Optional[PricingEntry]) -> Optional[_dt.date]:
+    """The entry's `price_date` as a date, or None when absent or not a valid `YYYY-MM-DD`."""
+    raw = getattr(entry, "price_date", None)

+    """True when the entry carries a `price_date` older than STALE_PRICE_DAYS (an entry without one is not stale:

+    date = price_date_of(entry)

+#

+# (with --json, one JSON object per line). Rates are the catalog's unit: micro-USD per million tokens. An alias with

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""hop-locality.py — classify model hops as local or hosted for `hounfour.locality: local_voices` (cycle-129 FR-8,
SDD D-8.0 / D-8.1, DEC-0146).

    python3 -I hop-locality.py --catalog <model-config.yaml> --config <.loa.config.yaml> -- <hop>...

One tab-separated line per hop, in the order given:

    <hop> TAB <provider|unknown> TAB <local|hosted> TAB <reason>

A hop is `local` only when ALL of these hold in the merged view (the System Zone catalog overlaid with the project
config's `hounfour.providers` / `hounfour.aliases`, the two layers cheval merges):
  * it resolves (a `provider:id` pin, an alias chain, or a bare id that exactly one provider declares) to a model entry
    that exists;
  * that model entry, or its provider block, says `dispatch_group: local` (the canonical key, D-8.0);
  * every hop on the entry's own `fallback_chain` is local by the same rule — cheval walks that chain inside one call,
    so a local entry that falls back to a hosted one would leave the declared providers without the planner seeing it.
Everything else is `hosted`: an unresolved hop, an unreadable config, a headless CLI hop (its dispatch group is the
provider family's), the native session. Fail closed — a hop is never called local because it could not be read.

This file reads declarations only: it never dispatches, never reads credentials and never imports the cheval package
(run under `-I`, so neither the cwd nor PYTHONPATH reaches sys.path). The request-time rules for a local hop (IP-literal
or localhost endpoint, no DNS, redirects refused, proxy env ignored, destination logged) are cheval's.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import sys
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple

MAX_DEPTH = 10


def _merge(base: Any, overlay: Any) -> Any:
    if isinstance(base, dict) and isinstance(overlay, dict):
        out = dict(base)
        for key, value in overlay.items():
            out[key] = _merge(base.get(key), value) if key in base else value
        return out
    return overlay


def load_merged(catalog_path: str, config_path: Optional[str]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    import yaml

    with open(catalog_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        catalog = yaml.safe_load(fh) or {}
    if not isinstance(catalog, dict):
        raise ValueError("catalog is not a mapping")
    merged: Dict[str, Any] = {k: (catalog.get(k) if isinstance(catalog.get(k), dict) else {})
                              for k in ("providers", "aliases", "backward_compat_aliases")}
    if config_path:
        try:
            with open(config_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
                project = yaml.safe_load(fh) or {}
        except FileNotFoundError:
            project = {}
        if not isinstance(project, dict):
            raise ValueError("project config is not a mapping")
        hounfour = project.get("hounfour")
        if isinstance(hounfour, dict):
            for key in ("providers", "aliases"):
                if isinstance(hounfour.get(key), dict):
                    merged[key] = _merge(merged.get(key) or {}, hounfour[key])
    return merged


def _alias_target(name: str, merged: Dict[str, Any]) -> Optional[str]:
    for table in ("aliases", "backward_compat_aliases"):
        target = (merged.get(table) or {}).get(name)
        if isinstance(target, dict):
            target = target.get("target") or target.get("model")
        if isinstance(target, str) and target.strip():
            return target.strip()
    return None


def resolve(hop: str, merged: Dict[str, Any]) -> Optional[Tuple[str, str]]:
    name = (hop or "").strip()
    if not name:
        return None
    current, seen = name, set()
    for _ in range(MAX_DEPTH):
        if ":" in current:
            provider, _, model = current.partition(":")
            return (provider, model) if provider and model else None
        target = _alias_target(current, merged)
        if not target:
            break
        if target in seen:
            return None
        seen.add(current)
        current = target
    if ":" in current:
        provider, _, model = current.partition(":")
        return (provider, model) if provider and model else None
    providers = merged.get("providers") or {}
    matches = [p for p, block in providers.items()
               if isinstance(block, dict) and isinstance(block.get("models"), dict) and current in block["models"]]
    return (matches[0], current) if len(matches) == 1 else None


def classify(hop: str, merged: Dict[str, Any], _depth: int = 0, _seen: Optional[set] = None) -> Tuple[str, str, str]:
    """(provider, locality, reason) for one hop."""
    seen = set(_seen or ())
    target = resolve(hop, merged)
    if target is None:
        return "unknown", "hosted", "unresolved"
    provider, model = target
    block = (merged.get("providers") or {}).get(provider)
    if not isinstance(block, dict):
        return provider, "hosted", "provider_not_declared"
    entry = (block.get("models") or {}).get(model) if isinstance(block.get("models"), dict) else None
    if not isinstance(entry, dict):
        return provider, "hosted", "model_not_declared"
    group = entry.get("dispatch_group") or block.get("dispatch_group") or ""
    if group != "local":
        return provider, "hosted", f"dispatch_group={group or 'unset'}"
    key = f"{provider}:{model}"
    if key in seen:
        return provider, "local", "dispatch_group=local"
    seen.add(key)
    chain = entry.get("fallback_chain") or []
    if not isinstance(chain, list):
        return provider, "hosted", "fallback_chain_unreadable"
    if _depth >= MAX_DEPTH:
        return provider, "hosted", "fallback_chain_too_deep"
    for nxt in chain:
        if not isinstance(nxt, str):
            return provider, "hosted", "fallback_chain_unreadable"
        p2, loc, _ = classify(nxt, merged, _depth + 1, seen)
        if loc != "local":
            return provider, "hosted", f"fallback_chain_reaches_hosted:{nxt}({p2})"
    return provider, "local", "dispatch_group=local"


def _clean(text: str) -> str:
    return "".join(c if c.isprintable() and c not in "\t" else "_" for c in text)[:128]


def main(argv: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("--catalog", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--config", default="")
    ap.add_argument("hops", nargs="*")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        merged = load_merged(args.catalog, args.config or None)
        err = ""
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — fail closed: every hop hosted, the reason said once
        merged, err = None, f"{type(exc).__name__}"
        print(f"hop-locality: the merged config could not be read ({err}) — every hop is hosted", file=sys.stderr)
    for hop in args.hops:
        if merged is None:
            print(f"{_clean(hop)}\tunknown\thosted\tconfig_unreadable")
            continue
        provider, loc, reason = classify(hop, merged)
        print(f"{_clean(hop)}\t{_clean(provider)}\t{loc}\t{_clean(reason)}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

1	"""Per-provider endpoint policy on the cheval Python path (cycle-129 FR-7, SDD D-7.2, D-8.0).
     2	
     3	The rule, applied at config load to every HTTP provider in the merged ``hounfour.providers`` view:
     4	
     5	* ``allow_insecure_endpoint`` is a host STRING, never a boolean. It must be an IP literal or ``localhost``
     6	  (an insecure endpoint is never resolved through DNS, so there is no rebinding), and the address must be
     7	  loopback (``127.0.0.0/8``, ``::1``) or RFC1918 (``10/8``, ``172.16/12``, ``192.168/16``). Link-local,
     8	  the cloud metadata addresses, unique-local IPv6 and every public range are refused.
     9	* An ``http://`` endpoint is admitted only when its host equals the provider's opt-in host. A mismatched
    10	  host, a public ``http`` host or an ``http`` endpoint without an opt-in fails at load with a named reason.
    11	* Every other endpoint keeps the cycle-099 refusals: ``https`` only, no userinfo, no control bytes or path
    12	  traversal, and no loopback, private, link-local, metadata or otherwise blocked IP literal (``localhost``
    13	  included). One provider's opt-in never changes another provider's checks.
    14	* ``keyless: true`` marks a provider that needs no credential; a literal ``auth: "local"`` is accepted and
    15	  normalised to ``keyless: true`` in the merged view. A keyless provider is admitted only when every model
    16	  declares ``context_window`` and ``dispatch_group``.
    17	
    18	ONE implementation: every URL and opt-in decision here is made by the canonical

class StreamingRecoveryTracker:
    """Stateful per-stream tracker. Initialize with config + start_time_s,
    then call ``on_token(text, now_s)`` for each token / ``check_deadline(now_s)``
    while waiting."""

    config: StreamingRecoveryConfig
    start_time_s: float
    tokens_seen: int = 0
    first_token_time_s: Optional[float] = None
    visible_content_seen: bool = False
    cot_prefix_buffer: str = ""

    def check_deadline(self, now_s: float) -> StreamingRecoveryDecision:
        """Call periodically while waiting for the first token. Returns
        abort decision if first_token_deadline elapsed without a token."""
        if self.first_token_time_s is not None:
            return StreamingRecoveryDecision.proceed()
        elapsed = now_s - self.start_time_s
        if elapsed >= self.config.first_token_deadline_s:
            return StreamingRecoveryDecision.abort_with(
                "first_token_deadline", tokens=0,
            )
        return StreamingRecoveryDecision.proceed()

    def on_progress(self, now_s: float) -> None:
        """Record stream progress that is NOT visible content (cycle-129 FR-7, SDD D-7.3):
        a `reasoning_content` delta from a local reasoning model. It satisfies the
        first-token deadline (the only wall-clock deadline the tracker keeps; the read
        timeout bounds a stall after the first byte) but leaves the content state
        machine alone: it does not count toward the empty-content window or mark
        visible content, and it is never part of the answer."""
        if self.first_token_time_s is None:
            self.first_token_time_s = now_s

    def on_token(self, text: str, now_s: float) -> StreamingRecoveryDecision:
        """Feed one token (or token-batch) of text. Returns abort
        decision when one of the empty-content or CoT-budget thresholds
        fires.

        State machine:
          - `visible_content_seen` starts False.
          - First non-empty token: if it matches CoT-prefix regex →
            engage CoT mode (in_cot_mode=True); else visible_content_seen=True.
          - Once in CoT mode: subsequent tokens stay in CoT until a
            structured-answer marker appears (JSON/array opener, ##
            heading, SEVERITY: marker, ``` fence, </thinking>).
          - Empty-content window: first N tokens all empty AND no
            visible content → abort.
          - CoT budget (reasoning-class only): tokens emitted in CoT
            mode exceed budget → abort.
        """
        if self.first_token_time_s is None:
            self.first_token_time_s = now_s
        self.tokens_seen += 1

        is_empty = not text or text.strip() == ""

        # State transition logic — only when we haven't seen visible
        # content yet AND token is non-empty
        if not is_empty and not self.visible_content_seen:
            if self._looks_like_answer_marker(text):
                # Structured-answer marker — exit CoT, mark visible
                self.visible_content_seen = True
            elif self._looks_like_cot(text):
                # CoT-shaped token (start OR continuation containing
                # thinking/let me/i'll/first I or <thinking>) —
                # accumulate into CoT buffer
                self.cot_prefix_buffer += text
            else:
                # Non-empty, not CoT, not structured marker — treat as
                # visible content (e.g., bare prose answer like
                # "Actual answer: 42")
                self.visible_content_seen = True

        # Empty-content window: first N tokens all empty/CoT-only → abort
        if (
            not self.visible_content_seen
            and self.tokens_seen >= self.config.empty_content_window_tokens
            and not self.cot_prefix_buffer
        ):
            return StreamingRecoveryDecision.abort_with(
                "empty_content_window",
                tokens=self.tokens_seen,
            )

        # CoT-budget: reasoning-class models that runaway-CoT without
        # visible content beyond budget → abort. We count TOKENS-IN-COT
        # rather than total tokens-seen so empty prefix doesn't trigger
        # this prematurely.
        if (
            self.config.reasoning_class
            and not self.visible_content_seen
            and self.cot_prefix_buffer
            and self.tokens_seen > self.config.cot_budget_tokens
        ):
            return StreamingRecoveryDecision.abort_with(
                "cot_budget_exhausted",
                tokens=self.tokens_seen,
            )

        return StreamingRecoveryDecision.proceed()

  local raw_response="$1"
  local type="$2"
  local model="$3"
  local sprint_id="$4"
  local api_exit_code="${5:-0}"
  local diff_files="$6"

  local timestamp
  timestamp=$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")

  # STATE 1: API failure
  if [[ "$api_exit_code" != "0" ]]; then
    local degraded="false"
    if [[ "$type" == "audit" ]]; then degraded="true"; fi
    jq -n \
      --arg type "$type" --arg model "$model" --arg sid "$sprint_id" \
      --arg ts "$timestamp" --argjson degraded "$degraded" \
      --arg err "API call failed with exit code $api_exit_code" \
      '{findings: [], metadata: {type: $type, model: $model, sprint_id: $sid,
3099:    res=$(process_findings "$raw" "$type" "$m" "$sprint_id" "$rc" "$diff_files") || res=""

_apply_hallucination_filter() {
    local result="$1"
    local diff_file="$2"

    # Defensive: missing diff file → emit metadata with reason, return.
    # G-6 (cycle-094): metadata is always present on the result; absence
    # was previously ambiguous between "filter not run" and "filter ran with
    # no downgrades". Now `applied: false, reason: "no_diff_file"` makes
    # the early-return state legible.
    if [[ -z "$diff_file" ]] || [[ ! -f "$diff_file" ]]; then
        printf '%s' "$result" | jq '.metadata.hallucination_filter = {applied: false, downgraded: 0, reason: "no_diff_file"}'
        return 0
    fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# session-cap-bb dispatcher.sh — phase 2 (dispatcher) for the post-reset
# bridgebuilder fan-out (bd-fanout-real-dispatch-9jv6 Tranche 1).
#
# On action:dispatch, fires the bridgebuilder-review headless entrypoint
# (resources/entry.sh — the same binary spiral-harness.sh already runs
# unattended) with --repo <owner/repo> and NO --pr, so BB self-discovers open
# PRs and dedups on its own incremental per-PR diff hashing. On action:noop it
# short-circuits (exit 0, nothing was in flight). This is the only mutating
# phase; a re-run under the same cycle_id re-invokes BB, whose per-PR hashing
# makes the review itself idempotent.
#
# Args: $1 cycle_id  $2 schedule_id  $3 phase_index  $4 prior_phases_json
set -euo pipefail

cycle_id="${1:?cycle_id required}"
schedule_id="${2:?schedule_id required}"

_here="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "${_here}/../../../../.." && pwd)"
# The scheduler canonicalizes phase paths through the consumer's skills mount.
# Rebind a physical .loa root only when that consumer mounts these same skills.
if [[ "${REPO_ROOT##*/}" == ".loa" &&
      "${REPO_ROOT}/../.claude/skills" -ef "${REPO_ROOT}/.claude/skills" ]]; then
    REPO_ROOT="$(cd "${REPO_ROOT}/.." && pwd)"
fi
_sanitize() { printf '%s' "$1" | tr -c 'A-Za-z0-9._-' '_'; }
HANDOFF_DIR="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/loa-session-cap-bb.$(_sanitize "$cycle_id")"
mkdir -p "$HANDOFF_DIR"
DECIDER_FILE="${HANDOFF_DIR}/decider.json"

write_out() { printf '%s' "$1" | tee "${HANDOFF_DIR}/dispatcher.json"; }

action="noop"
if [[ -f "$DECIDER_FILE" ]] && jq empty "$DECIDER_FILE" 2>/dev/null; then
    action="$(jq -r '.action // "noop"' "$DECIDER_FILE")"
fi

if [[ "$action" != "dispatch" ]]; then
    write_out "$(jq -nc --arg cid "$cycle_id" --arg sid "$schedule_id" \
        '{cycle_id:$cid, schedule_id:$sid, dispatched:false,
          reason:"nothing was in flight (decider noop)"}')"
    exit 0
fi

# Resolve owner/repo: explicit override wins, else derive from the git origin.
repo="${LOA_SESSION_CAP_BB_REPO:-}"
if [[ -z "$repo" ]]; then
    url="$(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" remote get-url origin 2>/dev/null || true)"
    repo="$(printf '%s' "$url" | sed -E 's#\.git$##; s#^.*[:/]([^/]+/[^/]+)$#\1#')"
fi
if [[ -z "$repo" ]]; then
    echo "dispatcher: could not resolve owner/repo (set LOA_SESSION_CAP_BB_REPO or a git origin)" >&2
    exit 1
fi

BB_ENTRY="${LOA_SESSION_CAP_BB_ENTRY:-${_here}/../../../bridgebuilder-review/resources/entry.sh}"
if [[ ! -f "$BB_ENTRY" ]]; then
    echo "dispatcher: bridgebuilder entrypoint not found: $BB_ENTRY" >&2
    exit 1

That holds even when the working-tree `.loa.config.yaml` says `local_voices`, and that working-tree file is the one cheval, adversarial-review.sh and flatline read. Bridgebuilder then sends the diff to hosted providers while every other gate stays local. A head that asks for the stricter posture should be honoured, and an unreadable trusted source should not quietly mean hosted.
head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/config.ts:684 — The head-only refusal only checks whether a provider newly gains `keyless` or `allow_insecure_endpoint`. Bridgebuilder voices are still dispatched by cheval, and cheval loads the PR head's `.loa.config.yaml`. So a head that changes the `endpoint` (or `auth` env) of a trusted keyless or `{env:…}` provider, or of a built-in one such as openai, to another https host passes this check: prompts and credentials go wherever the head says. The claim that providers are read "only from trusted configuration" therefore does not hold at dispatch time.
head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/config.ts:482 — Any literal non-`{env:` `auth` string is classed as keyless. cheval normalises only the literal `"local"` (endpoint_policy.py:50 KEYLESS_AUTH_LITERALS) and sends any other literal as a Bearer key. Bridgebuilder therefore labels such a provider keyless, admits it with no env var, and reports it in the "keyless providers" startup line, which disagrees with what cheval does.
head/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/config.ts:726 — `isLocalVoice` never looks at the model entry's `fallback_chain`. lib/hop-locality.py treats a local entry whose fallback chain reaches a hosted entry as hosted, because cheval walks that chain inside one call. Bridgebuilder plans such a voice as local, so under `local_voices` a hosted fallback can still be dispatched.
head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/audit/modelinv.py:476 — `hop_locality_of` reads `dispatch_group` from the model entry only. lib/hop-locality.py:116 and Bridgebuilder `isLocalVoice` also accept a provider-level `dispatch_group: local`. A hop the planners admitted as local under `local_voices` is then recorded in MODELINV as `hop_locality: hosted`, so the audit trail contradicts the plan.
head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/openai_adapter.py:221 — `_transport_policy` keys on the model-level `dispatch_group` only (cheval.py:541 copies only `model_data.get("dispatch_group")`). The three readers disagree about where the canonical key lives.
head/.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh:4266 — The comment says cheval enforces an "IP-literal or localhost endpoint, no DNS" rule on every local hop, but nothing does. hop-locality.py classifies on the declared `dispatch_group` alone. TransportPolicy only checks same-origin and path prefix, and `validate_declared_endpoint` accepts any public https host. A provider labelled `dispatch_group: local` with a hosted https endpoint therefore passes `local_voices` and receives the prompts. Either enforce a loopback/RFC1918 endpoint for local hops or correct the claim.

I've written the review to `/workspace/review.md`: 12 findings and **Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED**. I reviewed by reading the code. I didn't run the test suites, because `pr/` holds only the touched files, not a runnable repo. The only code I ran was a quick check that the new endpoint validator still accepts the default catalog endpoints, including Bedrock's `{region}` template; it does.

**What blocks the merge:**
